production.note: US model years. First: Lotus release of July 2019: "The new 2020 Lotus Evora GT can be ordered now for the USA and Canada." Last: Kelley Blue Book (a database) lists only the 2020 and 2021 model years and its 2022 address shows "Used 2021 Lotus Evora GT" (kbb-evora-gt-2021). Lotus's heritage page (lotus-evora-heritage) gives the Evora 400 range "Year of production 2015-2021". No Lotus page names 2021 as the last US model year.

body.note: Two-door mid-engined coupe, offered as a 2+2 or 2+0 ("Available in both 2 seat and 2+2 configurations", lotus-us-evora-gt-release-speedjournal).

configuration.note: "3.5 litre (3,456 cc) V6, 24-valve, water cooled, all aluminium engine, with Edelbrock supercharger"

displacementL.note: 3,456 cc, quoted from the Lotus specification table: "3.5 litre (3,456 cc) V6". Lotus's heritage page (lotus-evora-heritage) gives "Engine 3,456cc supercharged V6" for the Evora 400 range.

aspiration.note: "with Edelbrock supercharger"; the Lotus release also says "supercharged, 3.5-litre 6-cylinder engine with integrated water-to-air charge cooler"

drivetrain.note: Rear-wheel drive with a "Torsen Type Limited Slip Differential (manual only)"

transmission.note: Standard six-speed manual; optional "6-speed automatic transmission, with gearbox cooler, ultra-fast changes via steering wheel mounted lightweight aluminium paddles". Lotus release: "In addition to Lotus' slick, six-speed manual gearbox ... the Evora GT is also available with an automatic transmission option" (lotus-us-evora-gt-release-speedjournal).

powerHp.note: Quote (Lotus specification table for the North American Evora GT): "Max power | PS / bhp | 422 / 416 | 422 / 416" (manual and automatic columns). Lotus release (lotus-us-evora-gt-release-speedjournal): "producing 422 PS (416 bhp) at 7000 rpm". Lotus's rating is the metric 422 PS; 422 x 0.98632 = 416 hp, the figure Lotus prints as bhp for the US car, so powerStandard is DIN PS (as in the McLaren 720S record).

weightLb.note: Standard car, manual transmission. Quote (Lotus specification table, columns MANUAL and AUTOMATIC): "Wet / kerb weight | lbs / kg | 3,175 / 1440 | 3,199 / 1451". Lotus does not say whether this is a DIN figure. Jalopnik gives the same figure: "Curb weight stays at 3,175 pounds for the manual car" (jalopnik-evora-gt-2019). Lotus's lightest figures, "Lightest possible weight lbs / kg 3,104 / 1,408" ("With all the lightweight options fitted"), and 3,128 / 1,419 in the automatic column, are for optioned cars and not used.
